title: rules-protocol v1: shared definitions
description: Value types shared by every v1 schema. Money is ALWAYS an integer number of minor units of the document currency (ADR-008: CNY fen, JPY yen, KWD fils); rates and scale factors are decimal strings. No money or rate field is a JSON floating-point number. INPUT values are limited to the range the engine's CP-SAT model can represent (README: supported numeric range): money |v| <= 10^13 minor units, rates 0..1 with at most 5 decimals, scale factors 0..10, dates 1970-01-01..2999-12-31. RESULT money (sums such as balances) uses the full int64 range.

ProtocolVersion.description: Protocol version of the document. Validators reject any other value.

MinorAmount.description: Input money: signed integer minor units of the document currency, |v| <= 10^13 (the engine's variable bound BIG). An integer TOKEN: 1000000.0 is a float even where standard JSON Schema calls it an integer; every v1 validator redefines 'integer' accordingly (README).

NonNegativeMinorAmount.description: Input money: integer minor units, 0 <= v <= 10^13.

PositiveMinorAmount.description: Input money: integer minor units, 1 <= v <= 10^13.

ResultMinorAmount.description: Result money (may be a sum of input amounts, e.g. a balance): signed integer minor units within int64.

NonNegativeResultMinorAmount.description: Result money: integer minor units >= 0 within int64.

PositiveResultMinorAmount.description: Result money: integer minor units >= 1 within int64.

Int64.description: Integer that is not money (e.g. an objective value), within int64.

Date.description: Calendar date YYYY-MM-DD (business date in the account's time zone), years 1970..2999: the engine adds up to about two years to dates, far from the calendar's limits. The pattern bounds month and day; the 'date' format (checked by the runner) rejects impossible days such as 2026-02-30.

ResultDate.description: Date in a result: YYYY-MM-DD without the input year limit (derived dates such as due dates may lie up to about two years after the latest input date).

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit offset (Z or +hh:mm/-hh:mm up to 23:59) and at most 6 fractional digits, years 1970..2999; hours 00-23, minutes and seconds 00-59 (no leap second). Upper-case T and Z only. The pattern is normative; the 'date-time' format must be checked as well (impossible days such as 2026-02-30): the Python runner registers a standard-library check because jsonschema skips 'date-time' without rfc3339-validator.

Id.description: Identifier (UUIDs and short fixture ids alike): ASCII letters, digits and . _ : - ; starts with a letter or digit; at most 128 characters.

EventId.description: Cash event identifier. The prefix 'plan_repay_' is reserved for the repayment events the engine adds for a plan.

Rate.description: Rate as a decimal string in CANONICAL form, 0..1 with at most 5 fractional digits and no trailing zeros ('0.006', '0', '1'; never '0.00600' or '1.0'); never a JSON number. One value has one text, so equal rates give equal input hashes; a NUMERIC read from a database is written canonically before it enters a document. 5 digits is the most the CP-SAT fee/benefit constraints can carry next to 10^13 money (README: supported numeric range).

ScaleFactor.description: Scenario scale factor as a decimal string in CANONICAL form, 0..10 with at most 10 fractional digits and no trailing zeros ('1', '0.5', '10'; never '1.0'); never a JSON number.

SignedDecimalString.description: Decimal written as a string (derived quantities such as a weighted buffer in days).

Text.description: Free descriptive text; never interpreted by the engine. maxLength counts Unicode code points (an emoji is ONE; Dart: runes.length, not String.length), as JSON Schema does.
